quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that is a huge, spinning storm that forms over warm ocean water!
quests.question: Hurricane
quests.hint: This massive storm has a calm, quiet center called an eye, surrounded by powerful winds.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Hurricane is correct because it is a huge, spinning storm that forms over warm ocean water.
quests.funFact: The exact same kind of storm is called a typhoon or a cyclone in other parts of the world!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that falls as a mix of rain and tiny bits of ice!
quests.question: Sleet
quests.hint: This makes sidewalks extra slippery, more than plain rain or plain snow alone.
quests.explanation: Yes! Sleet is correct because it falls as a mix of rain and tiny bits of ice.
quests.funFact: Sleet forms when snowflakes partly melt, then freeze again before they reach the ground!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that is a sudden, strong burst of wind!
quests.question: Gust
quests.hint: This can suddenly snatch a hat right off someone's head.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Gust is correct because it is a sudden, strong burst of wind.
quests.funFact: A single strong gust of wind can be much faster than the steady breeze around it!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a tiny drop of water resting on grass in the early morning!
quests.question: Dewdrop
quests.hint: You'll often see these tiny, sparkly drops before the morning Sun dries them up.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Dewdrop is correct because it is a tiny drop of water resting on grass in the morning.
quests.funFact: Dewdrops form when warm air touches cool grass overnight and turns back into water!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a shallow patch of calm water separated from the sea by a reef!
quests.question: Lagoon
quests.hint: This calm, warm water is perfect for gently wading or snorkeling.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Lagoon is correct because it is a shallow, calm patch of water separated from the sea by a reef.
quests.funFact: Lagoons are often much warmer than the deep ocean because their water is so shallow!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a long, narrow strip of sea between tall, steep cliffs!
quests.question: Fjord
quests.hint: Ancient sliding ice once carved this deep, narrow waterway between the rocky cliffs.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Fjord is correct because it is a long, narrow strip of sea between tall, steep cliffs.
quests.funFact: Norway is famous for having some of the deepest and most beautiful fjords in the world!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object where a river's fresh water mixes with the sea's salty water!
quests.question: Estuary
quests.hint: Many young fish grow up safely in this calm, mixed water near the coast.
quests.explanation: Yes! An Estuary is correct because it is where a river's fresh water mixes with the sea's salty water.
quests.funFact: Estuaries are one of the richest places for wildlife because two kinds of water meet there!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a very young plant that has just grown its first tiny leaves!
quests.question: Seedling
quests.hint: This delicate little plant needs gentle care to survive its first few weeks.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Seedling is correct because it is a very young plant with just its first tiny leaves.
quests.funFact: A seedling's very first leaves often look different from the leaves it will grow later on!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is the sweet liquid flowers make to attract buzzing visitors!
quests.question: Nectar
quests.hint: Bees and butterflies travel from flower to flower searching for this sweet treat.
quests.explanation: Yes! Nectar is correct because it is the sweet liquid that flowers make to attract visitors.
quests.funFact: Bees turn the nectar they collect from flowers into the honey we love to eat!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a tree with an enormously thick trunk and short, spread-out branches!
quests.question: Baobab
quests.hint: This tree's huge trunk can store thousands of liters of water to survive the dry season.
quests.explanation: Yes! A Baobab is correct because it is a tree with an enormously thick trunk and short branches.
quests.funFact: Some baobab trees are thousands of years old and hollow enough to walk inside!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event with a calm, still center surrounded by powerful spinning winds!
quests.question: Hurricane
quests.hint: Warm ocean water gives this enormous storm all the energy it needs to grow.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Hurricane is correct because it has a calm center surrounded by powerful spinning winds.
quests.funFact: Hurricanes are given human names to make them easier to track and talk about!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that sounds like tiny pebbles tapping on a window!
quests.question: Sleet
quests.hint: This icy, wintry mix is somewhere between falling rain and falling snow.
quests.explanation: That's right! Sleet is correct because its icy mix taps against windows like tiny pebbles.
quests.funFact: Sleet bounces a little when it hits the ground, unlike soft, fluffy snow!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that can suddenly rattle windows or slam a door shut!
quests.question: Gust
quests.hint: This quick, powerful puff of wind comes and goes in just a moment.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Gust is correct because its sudden, powerful puff of wind can rattle windows or slam doors.
quests.funFact: Weather reporters measure the strongest gusts to warn people before a big storm arrives!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that glitters like a tiny jewel on a spiderweb at sunrise!
quests.question: Dewdrop
quests.hint: Spiderwebs look extra sparkly and beautiful when covered in hundreds of these tiny drops.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Dewdrop is correct because it glitters like a tiny jewel on webs and grass at sunrise.
quests.funFact: A single leaf can be covered in hundreds of tiny dewdrops on a cool morning!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is a peaceful, turquoise pool nearly closed off from ocean waves!
quests.question: Lagoon
quests.hint: A thin strip of sand or coral usually protects this calm water from rough waves.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Lagoon is correct because it is a peaceful pool of water nearly closed off from ocean waves.
quests.funFact: Some of the most beautiful lagoons in the world sit right in the middle of a coral atoll!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object formed long ago by a massive glacier carving through solid rock!
quests.question: Fjord
quests.hint: This deep, watery valley was carved out by slow-moving ice thousands of years ago.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Fjord is correct because a massive glacier carved it out of solid rock long ago.
quests.funFact: Some fjords are so deep that huge cruise ships can sail right between towering cliffs!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object found at the mouth of a river, right before it reaches the ocean!
quests.question: Estuary
quests.hint: The water here changes with the tide, becoming saltier or fresher throughout the day.
quests.explanation: That's right! An Estuary is correct because it is found at a river's mouth, right before it meets the ocean.
quests.funFact: Many busy port cities were built beside an estuary because ships can shelter there safely!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that grows in a small pot before being planted outside in a garden!
quests.question: Seedling
quests.hint: Gardeners often start these tiny, delicate plants indoors before the weather warms up.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Seedling is correct because it grows in a small pot before being planted outside.
quests.funFact: Many vegetable plants start as seedlings indoors, weeks before they're planted in an outdoor garden!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object hidden deep inside a flower, rewarding whoever visits it!
quests.question: Nectar
quests.hint: A hummingbird's long beak is perfectly shaped to reach this sweet liquid.
quests.explanation: That's right! Nectar is correct because it is the sweet reward hidden deep inside a flower.
quests.funFact: Some flowers only make their nectar at night, to attract moths instead of bees!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that looks like its roots are growing up into the sky instead of down!
quests.question: Baobab
quests.hint: This unusual-looking tree's bare branches can look upside-down during the dry season.
quests.explanation: That's right! A Baobab is correct because its bare branches can look like upside-down roots in the sky.
quests.funFact: People sometimes call the baobab the 'upside-down tree' because of its unusual shape!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that weather scientists track closely as it swirls across the ocean!
quests.question: Hurricane
quests.hint: This massive, swirling storm can stretch wider than an entire country.
quests.explanation: Great job! A Hurricane is correct because it is the massive, swirling storm that scientists carefully track.
quests.funFact: Hurricanes get weaker once they move over land, since they need warm ocean water for energy!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event where falling snowflakes melt partway, then refreeze into tiny ice pellets!
quests.question: Sleet
quests.hint: This wintry weather is trickier to walk in than snow because it's slicker underfoot.
quests.explanation: Great choice! Sleet is correct because its snowflakes melt partway, then refreeze into tiny ice pellets.
quests.funFact: Roads covered in sleet can be even more slippery than roads covered in regular snow!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature event that can suddenly push a kite higher without any warning!
quests.question: Gust
quests.hint: This burst of wind arrives quickly and just as quickly fades away again.
quests.explanation: Great job! A Gust is correct because it can suddenly push a kite higher with its quick burst of wind.
quests.funFact: The strongest wind gust ever measured was faster than many race cars!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that quietly disappears once the morning Sun warms the air!
quests.question: Dewdrop
quests.hint: This tiny drop of water only lasts until the morning warms up a little.
quests.explanation: Great choice! A Dewdrop is correct because it quietly disappears once the morning Sun warms the air.
quests.funFact: Some desert animals actually drink dewdrops to get water in the early morning!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object where colorful fish shelter in calm, shallow water near a reef!
quests.question: Lagoon
quests.hint: This calm water stays much gentler than the choppy, open sea nearby.
quests.explanation: Great job! A Lagoon is correct because colorful fish shelter in its calm, shallow water near a reef.
quests.funFact: Some lagoons change color throughout the day as the sunlight shifts overhead!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object where waterfalls tumble down steep cliffs into a deep, narrow sea inlet!
quests.question: Fjord
quests.hint: Boats sailing through here pass beneath towering rock walls on both sides.
quests.explanation: Great choice! A Fjord is correct because waterfalls tumble down its steep cliffs into the narrow inlet.
quests.funFact: The word 'fjord' comes from an old Norse word meaning a place you travel across!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that acts like a nursery for baby fish and shellfish near the coast!
quests.question: Estuary
quests.hint: This calm, mixed water provides food and shelter for many young sea creatures.
quests.explanation: Great job! An Estuary is correct because it acts like a nursery for baby fish and shellfish near the coast.
quests.funFact: Losing an estuary can hurt an entire coastline's fish population, since so many species depend on it!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that is too small and delicate to survive strong wind or frost just yet!
quests.question: Seedling
quests.hint: This young, tender plant needs protection until it grows a little bigger and stronger.
quests.explanation: Great choice! A Seedling is correct because it is too small and delicate to survive strong wind or frost yet.
quests.funFact: Only a small number of seedlings in the wild ever grow into a full, mature plant!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that gives bees and butterflies the energy they need to fly!
quests.question: Nectar
quests.hint: This sweet, sugary liquid is a flower's way of asking for help spreading its pollen.
quests.explanation: Great job! Nectar is correct because it gives bees and butterflies the energy they need to fly.
quests.funFact: A single bee might visit hundreds of flowers in one day, just searching for nectar!

quests.instruction: Identify the nature object that survives the dry season by storing water inside its giant trunk!
quests.question: Baobab
quests.hint: This tree's trunk can grow wider than a small car during its long lifetime.
quests.explanation: Great choice! A Baobab is correct because it survives the dry season by storing water in its giant trunk.
quests.funFact: Baobab trees grow mostly in Africa, Madagascar, and Australia!
